definitions.explanation: Handwriting that is messy, illegible, or lacking in aesthetic quality.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{悪筆|あくひつ}で{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: He is famous for his bad handwriting.

examples.japanese: {悪筆|あくひつ}で{読|よ}めない{字|じ}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: His handwriting is so bad that many characters are unreadable.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}の{処方箋|しょほうせん}が{悪筆|あくひつ}で、{薬剤師|やくざいし}が{読|よ}み{取|と}るのに{苦労|くろう}した。
examples.english: The doctor's prescription was so poorly written that the pharmacist had trouble reading it.

notes:
A compound of {悪|あく} (bad) + {筆|ひつ} (brush/writing). In Japan, where calligraphy ({書道|しょどう}) is part of school education, handwriting quality is taken more seriously than in many other cultures. Having {悪筆|あくひつ} can be seen as a minor social embarrassment.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {悪筆|あくひつ}で{有名|ゆうめい}: famous for bad handwriting
- {悪筆|あくひつ}を{直|なお}す: to fix one's bad handwriting
- ひどい{悪筆|あくひつ}: terrible handwriting

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {達筆|たっぴつ}: beautiful handwriting; fine penmanship — the opposite; a compliment for skilled calligraphy
- {癖字|くせじ}: idiosyncratic handwriting — not necessarily bad, just distinctive or hard for others to read
- {乱筆|らんぴつ}: messy writing — often used as a humble apology for one's own handwriting in letters
